Insulation workers (Insulation Workers, Floor, Ceiling, And Wall) are responsible for laying thermal and sound insulation materials on the walls, floors, ceilings and other parts of the building, cutting, installing and fixing the insulation layer according to the drawings and specifications to ensure that the thermal and acoustic performance meets the standards.

entries: Insulation workers are responsible for laying thermal and sound insulation materials on the walls, floors, ceilings and other parts of the building, cutting, installing and fixing the insulation layer according to the drawings and specifications to ensure that the thermal and acoustic performance meets the standards.
Measure the dimensions of walls, floors and ceilings according to the drawings, and calculate the amount of insulation material.
Cut glass wool, rock wool, foam board and other insulation materials and lay and fix them.
Treat joints, corners and wall penetrations of pipes to ensure a dense and continuous insulation layer.
Use mesh cloth, adhesive, insulation nails and other auxiliary materials to complete the reinforcement.
Implement dust protection and safety regulations for working at heights, and wear protective equipment.
Clean the work site, cooperate with inspection and acceptance and record the use of materials.

paragraphs: It usually takes two or three days to insulate a unit from floor to ceiling: first measure the size and draw lines, then use a special knife to cut the boards into appropriate shapes, stuff them into wooden keels or wall cavities piece by piece, fill the joints with glue, apply mesh cloth, and finally press and close the edges. After finishing a wall, just lean on it with a level and you will have an idea.

In a word: measure the size, cut the material, lay it out and fill it thoroughly. Specifically, it includes measurement and calculation, cutting and laying, joint reinforcement, pipeline processing, safety protection and on-site cleaning.

This line of work is suitable for people who are "steady-handed and careful, and can endure the dust" - they do work that is invisible, but each layer is laid into the bones of the house.

The most rewarding part of this business is the "visible effect": after the work is completed, scan it with an infrared camera and see that the wall is evenly colored in the thermal image, which means that the insulation layer you laid has no cavities or gaps - that sense of "it's accurate under your hands" is very real.
If you can accept "being gray but knowing" - every wall is a work of your own hands, this business is most likely suitable for you.
